title: Map the user journey end to end
summary: A journey map shows every step a user takes to reach their goal, including steps outside your product. It reveals where the experience breaks and makes sure the design solves the whole problem, not just one screen.

beginner: Choose one type of user and one goal, for example 'a new customer setting up their first account'.
List every step they take from start to finish, including emails, phone calls and offline steps.
For each step, note what they are doing, thinking and feeling, using research evidence.
Mark the pain points and moments that matter most.
Add the behind-the-scenes steps your organisation or systems take.
Mark where your chosen solution changes the journey, and check nothing breaks before or after it.
intermediate: Map the current journey for one user type and goal, using research evidence.
Include touchpoints outside the product and the behind-the-scenes processes.
Highlight pain points and map the future journey with the chosen concept.
Share the map and use it to scope the work.
experienced: Map journeys for the main user segments and show where they differ.
Connect journey pain points to data and to the business processes behind them.
Use the future journey to spot dependencies on other teams and systems early.
Make the journey map a shared artefact that guides prioritisation across teams.

canDelegateTo.task: Draw the current and future journey maps
Supply research evidence for each step
Map the behind-the-scenes processes and systems

toolExamples.miro: Use a journey map template with lanes for actions, thoughts, feelings, pain points and back-stage processes.
toolExamples.mural: Build the map with the team and add research quotes on each step.
toolExamples.figma: Create a polished version of the map to share with stakeholders.
toolExamples.claude: Paste research notes and ask it to draft the steps of the journey, then check every step against the evidence.

definitionOfDone: Current journey mapped with evidence and pain points
Future journey shows how the chosen concept changes it
Map shared and used to agree scope
pitfalls: Mapping only the steps inside your product
Filling the map with assumptions instead of research
Making the map once and never using it again
